the nexus of blockchain technology and whole genome sequencing (a) offers the promise of improved food safety by enhancing the ability of public health and industry actors to identify and prevent foodborne illness, but also (b) raises novel technical, governance, and regulatory challenges that require flexible and agile approaches to regulation, (c) which should include voluntary regulatory programs, technical standards, and soft law instruments, and (d) which should be responsive to the unique characteristics of blockchain and WSG technologies.
the convergence of blockchain and whole-genome sequencing (WGS), two emerging food safety technologies, could enhance regulatory capacity to respond to and mitigate foodborne illnesses.
the convergence of blockchain and WGs raises novel technical, policy, and governance challenges that can be addressed through flexible regulatory approaches.

the governance of emerging technologies that are likely to have a significant impact on food safety and public health.

the governance implications of blockchain for food safety and public health, and the extent to which blockchain may facilitate the adoption of whole genome sequencing (a technology that is already used by government and industry) for food safety purposes.
the governance of the intersection of two emerging technologies: WGS and blockchain.
